text:
Carlos (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands. Leaving a live thread here for follow-ups on security/compliance items (SOC2/ISO, VPC/private deployments, audit logs, KMS/BYOK). Drop questions and we'll loop in owners.

Grace (Security): Quick summary from my side — SOC2 scope will cover hosted API + control plane; Dedicated and Private are in scope for config/service controls but may need customer attestations for their infra. ISO work is starting next quarter; timeline is ~6-9 months.

Maya (Eng): For Private/VPC: is the control plane still Redwood-managed or customer-run? We had a few customers ask about full control plane isolation.

Grace (Security): Good q — default Private offering keeps a customer-dedicated control plane managed by Redwood inside your VPC (we run the control plane in your VPC via managed connectors). We also have an on-prem install option where customers run the control plane themselves (air-gapped).

Sam (SRE): Audit logs — what do we retain by default and how can customers pull them? Is forwarding to customer SIEM supported?

Grace (Security): Default hosted retention: 90 days of detailed audit logs in our console; aggregated events longer. For Dedicated/Private you can configure forwarding to customers' SIEM (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk/Datadog). Extended retention and egressed copies are available as an add-on.

Jorge (Privacy): Also adding — we support per-tenant export and data deletion APIs for customer request workflows (GDPR/CCPA). We'll produce deletion proof artifacts when requested.

Alex (Product): KMS/BYOK — can Private customers bring their own HSM keys? Also curious about FIPS/HSM posture for Dedicated.

Grace (Security): Yes. BYOK supported for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured to use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS / Google KMS / Azure Key Vault). For high-assurance customers we support HSM-backed keys and key-wrapping via CloudHSM/Azure Dedicated HSM. Hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys by default but we offer envelope encryption and dedicated customer keys for enterprise contracts.

Maya (Eng): Any docs or sample CLI to show how to register a customer key?

Grace (Security): We'll post a how-to in #docs shortly but here's a quick snippet for registering an AWS KMS key (example):
```
redwood private kms register --provider aws --key-arn arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
```
You'll also need to grant the Redwood service principal Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions.

Sam (SRE): On incident evidence — if a customer asks for timeline + raw audit events for an outage, what's the SLA to provide that?

Grace (Security): For customers with an enterprise contract / Dedicated we're committing to a 72-hour evidence package turnaround for incidents (includes raw audit logs, exportable traces, and config snapshots). For hosted customers it's case-by-case, but we can provide redacted audit exports within 7 days.

Carlos (CEO): Are there any blockers on publishing a public compliance portal (SOC2 cert, ISO progress, list of sub-processors)?

Grace (Security): Not blockers, just verification steps. We're finalizing the SOC2 Type II audit report and expect to publish a summary + download option in the compliance portal once it's cleared by legal. Sub-processor list will be posted and updated quarterly.

Jorge (Privacy): Small ask — can we add a short FAQ about what 'in scope' means for customers who self-host parts of their infra? Lots of customers misinterpret SOC2 scope.

Grace (Security): Agree. We'll draft an FAQ clarifying shared responsibility matrix (who controls physical/host infra vs Redwood-managed services) and examples. I'll ping the docs team to make this a short page + matrix.

Alex (Product): Roadmap ask — can we include a toggle for customers to opt into longer audit retention from the console (self-serve billing)? Might reduce ops tickets.

Maya (Eng): Also can we expose a log-forwarding webhook for lightweight customers who don't want a SIEM integration?

Sam (SRE): +1 to both. Less manual work on tickets.

Grace (Security): Noted. We'll scope both as product backlog items — rough ETA for design: 1 sprint; implementation depends on priority.

Carlos (CEO): Great thread — @Grace @Jorge let's consolidate answers and publish a follow-up doc with timelines. If folks have specific customer asks, paste them here and we'll prioritize. :thumbsup:
